components.role: Performs causal interventions such as activation patching to identify and analyze internal representation pathways and knowledge locations.
Decomposes internal representations into interpretable latent features to locate knowledge-bearing components.
Serves as the underlying model whose internal factual and reasoning knowledge is elicited.

target_task.text: Eliciting latent knowledge in large language models where internal facts are not faithfully reflected in surface-level outputs.

limitation.text: Existing approaches rely on contrastive activation patterns and struggle with complex multi-step reasoning tasks, while mechanistic interpretability tools are typically used to understand model behavior rather than extract hidden knowledge.

combination.text: The framework uses sparse autoencoder feature analysis and activation patching to locate knowledge-bearing representations inside the large language model, then applies causal probing to verify genuine latent knowledge and representation engineering to surface it without modifying model weights.

summary.text: This briefing analyzes combining patching, sparse autoencoders, and large language models for eliciting latent knowledge when internal facts are not reflected in surface outputs, integrating tools from paper:2605.28825. Patent assignees categorized as companies (patent:12229040) indicate commercial interest in automated code fixing and AI pipelines, while repositories like repo:eleutherai/sae-auto-interp and repo:gnueaj/unlearning-depth-score provide open-source implementations for interpretability and activation patching.

target_user.text: AI engineering teams, security practitioners, and automated software repair tool developers as supported by corporate patent assignees (patent:12229040) and specialized open-source repository contributors (repo:eleutherai/sae-auto-interp, repo:gnueaj/unlearning-depth-score).

jtbd.text: Eliciting hidden factual and reasoning knowledge from large language models when their surface outputs are incorrect or evasive, using sparse autoencoders and activation patching without modifying model weights as described in paper:2605.28825.

value_prop.text: Overcomes the limitations of contrastive activation patterns and complex multi-step reasoning failures by bridging mechanistic interpretability and latent knowledge elicitation, achieving an average elicitation accuracy of 84.7 percent on benchmarks like TruthfulQA as shown in paper:2605.28825.

riskiest_assumption.text: Users are willing to adopt a complex interpretability-based pipeline rather than standard weight-modification techniques to elicit latent knowledge, reflecting the lowest DVF score on axis D (desirability: 2.0).

mvp.text: A demand landing page outlining the mechanistic knowledge elicitation framework coupled with problem interviews targeting AI security and interpretability practitioners to test the desirability assumption (dvf:5).
mvp.type: demand landing page and problem interviews

success_metric.text: A proposed threshold of 30 percent conversion on the demand landing page or a proposed threshold of 70 percent positive validation from problem interviews regarding the need for weight-free latent knowledge extraction (dvf:5).

kill_criteria.text: Fewer than a proposed threshold of 5 percent of interviewed practitioners express willingness to adopt a separate interpretability pipeline over standard fine-tuning (dvf:5).
Landing page conversion stays below a proposed threshold of 2 percent after targeted outreach (dvf:5).

open_source.use: Deploys automated interpretability features to let language models analyze their own sparse autoencoder representations as cited in repo:eleutherai/sae-auto-interp.
Measures the depth of internal representations via activation patching to locate target knowledge components as described in repo:gnueaj/unlearning-depth-score.

to_build.text: A unified three-stage orchestration pipeline that connects sparse autoencoder feature analysis, causal probing verification, and weight-free representation engineering as outlined in paper:2605.28825.
